newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police suspect Palestinians in stabbings.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police suspect Palestinians in stabbings.

text.p: Israeli police said on Saturday they were checking whether two women whose bodies were found in the West Bank on Friday were killed by Palestinian guerrillas, although they didn't rule out criminal motives.

The chief of Israeli police in the West Bank told Army Radio police and army forces were searching the Wadi Qelt nature reserve where the stabbed bodies were found for footprints, evidence or witnesses.
"We are talking about an area where in the past there were attacks by Palestinian guerrillas," said police commander Yossi Sidbon.
Asked what indication there was that Palestinians could have committed the murders, Sidbon said:
"The stabbing, the place of the murder which is not a place for hikes and is not near criminal elements. We are checking a nationalist motive but do not rule out criminal activity."

One of the victims was identified as 23-year-old Hagit Zavitsky of the nearby Jewish settlement Kfar Adumim. Police did not release the name of the other victim who Sidbon said was believed to be Zavitsky's friend and hiking mate.
Police had said on Friday that the victims were teenagers.
Sidbon said Israeli police might ask Palestinian police, in charge of the nearby Jericho self-rule enclave, to cooperate in the investigation.
Jibril Rajoub, head of the Palestinian Preventive Security in the West Bank, told Reuters he had received no request from the Israelis.
A senior PLO official who asked not to be named said: "The Israelis always accuse the Palestinians when such incidents take place."
In July 1995, two Israelis were found in the Wadi Qelt area shot and stabbed to death in an unsolved case. In October 1993, Palestinian guerrillas killed two Israeli hikers in Wadi Qelt.
